graph.summary: Trastuzumab → Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 → cell population proliferation → Breast Neoplasms

evidence.snippet: Trastuzumab bound to HER2 specifically and with high affinity.
evidence.explanation: Direct binding of trastuzumab to HER2 was demonstrated in CHO cells expressing human HER2, confirming that trastuzumab molecularly interacts with the ERBB2/HER2 receptor.

paper.title: The effects of trastuzumab on HER2-mediated cell signaling in CHO cells expressing human HER2.

evidence.snippet: Overexpression of CHK mimics trastuzumab treatment to mediate ErbB2-Y1248 phosphorylation, Akt downregulation, and growth inhibition of trastuzumab-sensitive breast cancer cells.
evidence.explanation: Trastuzumab binding to ERBB2 leads to downstream Akt downregulation and growth inhibition, indicating that trastuzumab decreases the effective oncogenic activity of the ERBB2 receptor in HER2-positive breast cancer cells.

paper.title: Trastuzumab-induced recruitment of Csk-homologous kinase (CHK) to ErbB2 receptor is associated with ErbB2-Y1248 phosphorylation and ErbB2 degradation to mediate cell growth inhibition.

evidence.snippet: Trastuzumab partially decreased PI3K but not mTOR activity.
evidence.explanation: Trastuzumab reduces PI3K activity downstream of ERBB2, supporting that it decreases ERBB2-mediated signaling activity.

paper.title: Inhibition of mammalian target of rapamycin is required for optimal antitumor effect of HER2 inhibitors against HER2-overexpressing cancer cells.
paper.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research

evidence.snippet: HER2 is a receptor tyrosine kinase that activates downstream signalling pathways involved in cellular survival, growth and proliferation.
evidence.explanation: ERBB2/HER2 is described as directly activating downstream signaling that drives cell growth and proliferation, establishing ERBB2 as a positive regulator of cell population proliferation.

paper.title: The role of autophagy in HER2-targeted therapy.

evidence.snippet: Inhibition of HER2 signalling results in a reduction of tumour cell proliferation, invasiveness and survival.
evidence.explanation: The inverse relationship is stated directly — blocking HER2 signaling reduces tumour cell proliferation — confirming that HER2 signalling positively regulates tumour cell proliferation.

paper.title: Pertuzumab: a review of its use for first-line combination treatment of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.

evidence.snippet: HER2 overexpression reverses the proliferation inhibition caused by CAND1 loss both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence.explanation: HER2-driven cell proliferation restores tumor growth in HER2-positive breast cancer models both in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating that cell population proliferation is a key contributor to HER2-positive breast cancer progression.

paper.title: CAND1 mediates CUL7-dependent HER2 protein stability to drive breast cancer progression.

evidence.snippet: Amplification of the gene and subsequent overexpression of the HER2 protein lead to increased activation of downstream signalling and are implicated in several cancer types.
evidence.explanation: HER2 amplification leads to increased downstream signaling including cell proliferation, which is implicated in breast cancer (among other cancer types), supporting that cell proliferation contributes to HER2-positive breast cancer.

paper.title: The role of autophagy in HER2-targeted therapy.
